the microalbuminuria is not an independent predictor of renal impairment in hypertension.
microalbuminurea in hypertensive patients is associated with endothelial dysfunction and renal impairment but not with inflammation.

microalbumin is a marker of endothelial dysfunction in primary hypertension and it may contribute to the renal impairment in these patients.

The main takeaway from our work is that
microalbuminuric hypertension, even in the absence of diabetes, is associated with renal dysfunction.
microalbuminuric patients with uncomplicated primary hypertension are at risk for renal impairment and this risk seems to be independent of inflammation and endothelial dysfunction in the forearm.
